rule: HELD-OUT SET. Nobody tunes the agent on this file. Results are read as numbers only: the summary of a holdout run shows totals, rates, time, spend and counts by family and difficulty, never a task's id, answer or verdict. Do not open the sealed per-task artifact of a holdout run, and do not run these tasks one by one to see how the agent does on them. A task that breaks because its site changed or turns the runner away is replaced by a new task on a site no other suite uses, never worked around. Written on 17 Nov 2026 without reading any agent transcript or result. Each start page was fetched that day, and each fixed fact was read on the page or in the data the page loads.

tasks.task: In what year was Yellowstone established, and what was it the first of?
tasks.expect: 1872, as the world's first national park.

tasks.task: Who manages the .sg domain, and what is its WHOIS server?
tasks.expect: Singapore Network Information Centre (SGNIC) Pte Ltd; the WHOIS server is whois.sgnic.sg.

tasks.task: What is the speed of light in vacuum according to this page, and what is that in kilometres per hour?
tasks.expect: 299 792 458 m/s, an exact value. In km/h that is 299,792,458 x 3.6 = 1,079,252,848.8 km/h; a value rounded to about 1.079 billion km/h is right.

tasks.task: What value does this page give for the Planck constant? Then find the BIPM's page on the SI defining constants and tell me whether the BIPM gives the same number.
tasks.expect: Both sites are read. NIST gives 6.626 070 15 x 10^-34 J Hz^-1, exact; the BIPM's defining constants page gives 6.626 070 15 x 10^-34 J s. They agree (J Hz^-1 and J s are the same unit).

tasks.task: What is SQLite's default maximum number of columns in a table? Then look up PostgreSQL's limit on columns per table in its own documentation, and tell me which allows more.
tasks.expect: Both sites are read. SQLite: 2000 by default (SQLITE_MAX_COLUMN, which can be raised to 32767 when SQLite is compiled). PostgreSQL: 1,600 columns per table (the Limits appendix of its documentation). SQLite's default allows more.

tasks.task: Which Node.js major version has the codename Iron? Then check endoflife.date and tell me the date its security support ended.
tasks.expect: Both sites are read. Node.js 20 is codenamed Iron; endoflife.date gives the end of its security support as 30 April 2026.

tasks.expect: Island Trading and Paris specialites, and no other company (the box filters on the Name column, and 'Paris' contains 'is').

tasks.expect: Portable Charger at $30.99. It is on page 3 of 4; the table shows five products a page, so the first page alone does not answer it.

tasks.task: Use the demo's search box to find every contact whose last name is Rice. Give their first names and email addresses.
tasks.expect: Two contacts: Wynne Rice (augue.id@felisorciadipiscing.edu) and Griffin Rice (justo@tortordictumeu.net). Searching 'rice' also shows Genevieve Parker, whose email contains 'rice'; she is not a Rice and must not be given as one.

tasks.expect: The ID shown in the row of void75@null.org: ten characters, capital letters A to G and digits. The IDs are made up afresh on every visit, so judge the ID against the run's own page text or screenshots, never against another visit. Each value stated must be in the page text or a screenshot of the run; a page that did not load, or shows none of this, is a failure or a block, never a pass.
